newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gilts vulnerable to downside, eye 113-23.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gilts vulnerable to downside, eye 113-23.

text.p: British gilts will labour under a slight bear bias on Wednesday and may target 113-23 support, technical analysts said.
But any fall will be muted and the market will soon look to bounce back towards initial resistance at 114-11, they added.
"Gilts are trading in a small descending channel on daily charts and I think they will continue to hug that," said Elizabeth Miller, technical analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
"We will probably trade between 114-11 on the top side and 113-23 on the downside. We may edge a bit a lower but it won't be anything too aggressive -- there's a slight bear bias."
By 0710 GMT, September gilts were up 2/32 at 114-06.

Miller said Tuesday's dip through key support at 113-31, the low last Friday, had introduced the bearish tone. She said any move below 113-23, an area of congestion on daily and weekly charts, would run into key trendline support at 113-12.
"But for the moment, I think 113-23 will hold for today and we could see a bounce," said Miller.
She said if the market could claw back 114-11, it would head towards minor retracement at 114-27.
Juliette Clark, senior treasury manager at the Royal Bank of Scotland, was slightly more optimistic.
She said the market would trade between 114-04 and 114-11 ahead of the UK labour market data due 0830 GMT.
"Given the bullish state of the indicators, a break out of this range should be on the upside, and if this occurs, then congestion resistance at 114-17/18 will become the target," she said in a note.

That level is key on Wednesday, said Clark. If it forms a strong barrier, the market will remain under a short term bear threat, but if it breaks to the upside, it will signal the return of significant buying interest. She put next resistance at 114-25, then the top of the range at 115-00 to 115-05.
By 0725 GMT, December short sterling was unchanged at 92.60.
